generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small amount of oxygen or nitrogen into the magnetic high-entropy alloy can increase the coercive field by creating ordered interstitial complexes that impede dislocation motion and enhance strain hardening.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or as-sintered magnetic high-entropy alloy
generation.intervention: Interstitial doping with oxygen or nitrogen
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, as no records judged to transfer
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased coercive field by 10-20% compared to the baseline
generation.boundary: Doping levels above 1 at.% may lead to decreased coercive field due to over-saturation of interstitial sites
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of oxygen or nitrogen required to achieve the optimal coercive field is uncertain and requires further experimentation

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the coercive field of the doped and undoped magnetic high-entropy alloys using a vibrating sample magnetometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the doped alloy is not significantly higher than that of the undoped alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
